In the right figure, the height of the head top of the sleeping cat on the table is T+L, and the height of the head top of the sitting cat on the ground is S, so T+L-S=110. Adding the two equations gives 2T=150+110=260, therefore T=130. The height of the table is 130 cm.

method.method_draft: Use a midpoint/cancellation interpretation without separately solving for both cat heights. From the image, see that swapping the sitting and sleeping cats changes the measured distance by the posture-height difference in opposite directions. The 150 cm distance equals the table height plus the excess height of the sitting cat over the sleeping cat; the 110 cm distance equals the table height minus that same excess. Therefore the table height is exactly the average of the two measured distances: (150 + 110) / 2 = 130 cm.

Image description: The image has two relevant setups. In the right setup, the cats are swapped: the sleeping cat is on the table and the sitting cat is on the floor; the vertical distance between their tops is labeled 110 cm.

Reasoning: Let the table height be H. The sitting cat is taller than the sleeping cat by some posture-height excess x. In the left setup, the measured distance is the table height plus this excess, so H + x = 150. In the right setup, swapping the cats makes the excess count in the opposite direction, so H - x = 110. Adding the two measurements cancels the cat posture difference: 2H = 150 + 110 = 260, so H = 130 cm.
